name: calibration_v1
purpose: Frozen dataset for studying unknown/out-of-scope rejection -- NOT for reporting accuracy. Separate from benchmark_v1 and must never be used to tune or select the classifier itself; it exists to characterize the similarity-score distributions a rejection rule would threshold on.

category_definitions.known_holdout: The 50 trained species, research-grade, held out from BOTH training and benchmark_v1. Baseline for FALSE REJECTION rate: a good photo of a known species that a rejection rule incorrectly rejects.
category_definitions.out_of_scope_ant: Formicidae species NOT among the 50 (excluded via without_taxon_id on all 50 known taxon_ids), research-grade, sampled across as many distinct species as available (165 species for 300 images). The main case: an ant the model was never trained to recognize.
category_definitions.non_ant_insect: Non-Formicidae Insecta, research-grade, across 122 species. 'Pointed the app at the wrong bug' case.
category_definitions.unrelated: Non-insect photos -- Aves, Plantae, Mammalia in equal thirds, research-grade, across 119 species combined. Sanity-check case, expected to be the easiest to reject.
category_definitions.low_quality_known: EXPLORATORY -- not a controlled ground-truth class. Photos of the 50 species sourced from quality_grade=needs_id (not research), pooled ~10/species (463 candidates), then kept only if in the blurriest 150 by a measured Laplacian-variance sharpness score (see scrape_calibration.py:blur_score -- images capped to 512px before scoring). 'needs_id' means the community has NOT reached research-grade consensus on the species identification -- the species label on these rows is the OBSERVER'S claim, not verified species-level ground truth the way research-grade labels are. Two separate reasons a needs_id photo might fail to reach research grade: it's genuinely blurry/unusable (the property this category is trying to sample), or it's actually misidentified. This category cannot distinguish those two cases, so it is DIAGNOSTIC ONLY: never used as positive ground truth in any false-rejection calculation, and its label should be read as 'probably this species' rather than confirmed. See threshold_selection_policy below.

source: iNaturalist API (api.inaturalist.org/v1/observations), quality_grade as noted per category
exclusion_criteria: Structural: only observations created on/after 2026-06-16 were eligible -- the same cutoff benchmark_v1 uses, one day past training's wave-2 completion (2026-06-14 16:49 -04:00). An observation that did not exist at training scrape time cannot be a photo training saw.
Explicit exclusion against the training manifest's photo_id column (9989 ids) before any candidate was kept.
Explicit exclusion against benchmark_v1's photo_id AND observation_uuid columns (1591 each) before any candidate was kept -- calibration_v1 and benchmark_v1 are two disjoint frozen sets.
Verified zero overlap after the fact on three independent axes against BOTH training and benchmark_v1: photo_id, observation_uuid, and sha256 image hash (see verification block below).

verification.method: Training photo_id -> observation_uuid reused the reconstruction already built for benchmark_v1's verification (99.3% coverage, 9920/9989). Training image sha256 reused the hashes already computed from the 9981 locally cached files under data/clean/. benchmark_v1's photo_id/observation_uuid/sha256 were read directly from its own committed CSV.
verification.note: One internal duplicate was found and removed before this count: a known_holdout candidate (leptomyrmex-erythrocephalus, photo_id 693315171) turned out to be byte-identical to a DIFFERENT photo_id already in benchmark_v1 (691253248) -- the same photographer's photo re-submitted as a second iNat observation, the same phenomenon found and fixed in benchmark_v1 itself last session, this time surfacing as a cross-set collision instead of an intra-set one. Neither photo_id nor observation_uuid caught it; only the sha256 check did. Original scrape yielded 1006 images; final calibration_v1 is 1005.

threshold_selection_policy.positive_ground_truth_for_false_rejectio: known_holdout ONLY (research-grade). low_quality_known must never be used as the positive class for FRR -- its species labels are not verified (see category_definitions.low_quality_known).
threshold_selection_policy.negative_ground_truth_for_false_acceptan: out_of_scope_ant, non_ant_insect, unrelated (all research-grade, all species-level identifications).
threshold_selection_policy.low_quality_known_role: diagnostic only -- reported alongside the FRR/FAR curve to show whether a bad photo of a known species is distinguishable from a genuinely unknown species using similarity alone, never scored as a correct/incorrect rejection.
threshold_selection_policy.data_separation: calibration_v1 is for CHOOSING a rejection rule (distributions, tradeoff curve, threshold selection). It must not also be used to report the frozen rule's final performance -- that would let the same data both pick and grade the rule. Once a threshold is frozen, build unknown_test_v1 for final evaluation: a separate frozen set whose out-of-scope AND non-ant/unrelated images are disjoint from calibration_v1 not just at the image/observation level (already required) but at the SPECIES level for out_of_scope_ant -- different non-known ant species than the 165 sampled here, so the frozen rule is tested on species it was never calibrated against, not just fresh photos of the same 165.
threshold_selection_policy.benchmark_v1_is_unrelated: benchmark_v1 measures classification accuracy among the 50 known species and must never be modified or used to choose this threshold; the two are independent measurements.

frozen_candidate_abstention_threshold.status: CANDIDATE -- NOT VALIDATED, NOT APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION
frozen_candidate_abstention_threshold.must_not_be_implemented_yet: This threshold must NOT be implemented in api/inference.py or the mobile app. It is a candidate selected from calibration_v1 alone and has not been evaluated on any independent held-out set.
frozen_candidate_abstention_threshold.rule: abstain (do not present a species identification) when max_sim < 0.60; otherwise allow closest-match presentation
frozen_candidate_abstention_threshold.signal: max cosine similarity to any of the 50 class prototypes, raw cosine, no geo re-ranking
frozen_candidate_abstention_threshold.selected_using: calibration_v1 (this file's dataset) -- known_holdout, out_of_scope_ant, non_ant_insect, unrelated categories; low_quality_known was NOT used to select it (see threshold_selection_policy)

measured_behavior_at_0.60.note: Ground truth: known_holdout (research-grade) only for the known-species side; out_of_scope_ant for the OOD side. See calibration_v1_scores.json and the Phase B report for full detail.
measured_behavior_at_0.60.interpretation: Behaves as a confidence/abstention gate (meaningfully improves accuracy among accepted known-species predictions, and rejects incorrect predictions 3x more often than correct ones) rather than a reliable unknown-species detector (still accepts close to half of out-of-scope ant photographs -- AUC known-vs-out_of_scope_ant is only 0.660, the weakest of the three OOD categories).

frozen_candidate_abstention_threshold.validation_requirement: Must be evaluated EXACTLY ONCE on a future unknown_test_v1 whose out-of-scope ant SPECIES (not just images or observations) are disjoint from calibration_v1's 165 out-of-scope-ant species, before any production use. Do not modify this threshold after seeing unknown_test_v1 results -- if 0.60 performs poorly there, that is a finding to report, not a cue to re-tune against the same calibration data (see threshold_selection_policy .data_separation).

machine_readable_rule.signal: raw max cosine similarity before geo re-ranking
machine_readable_rule.note: Added for machine-readable provenance after the fact -- the original 0.60 selection and the original unknown_test_v1 one-pass evaluation both used this same value as a hardcoded constant in eval_unknown_test.py, not loaded from this file. eval_unknown_test.py was updated after that evaluation to load and validate this value for future reproductions; the rule itself (0.60, max_sim < value) is unchanged.

phase_c_validation.status: INDEPENDENTLY VALIDATED as a selective confidence/abstention gate; NOT VALIDATED as an unknown-species detector
phase_c_validation.must_not_be_adjusted_using_unknown_test_: 0.60 must not be adjusted, re-tuned, or re-derived using unknown_test_v1 results. unknown_test_v1 exists to grade this exact value once; if it performs poorly, that is a finding to report, not a cue to pick a new threshold from the same data (see threshold_selection_policy).
phase_c_validation.evaluated_on: data/unknown_test_v1/ (see unknown_test_v1.json for methodology and verification, unknown_test_v1_eval.json for full per-image results)

known_holdout_species_coverage.note: These 5 species have zero unknown_test_v1 known_holdout images (same low-observation-velocity species thin throughout this project's iNat-based sets). Their rejection/abstention behavior at 0.60 is entirely unmeasured, not merely under-sampled.

phase_c_validation.interpretation: At the frozen 0.60 threshold, 91/200 out-of-scope ant photographs (45.5%) still passed the gate and would receive one of the 50 supported species as their closest match, even though their true species is outside the catalog. Therefore this rule is useful as a selective confidence/quality gate but does not reliably detect unsupported ant species. This is a per-image rate measured across 127 distinct out-of-scope-ant species (species-disjoint from calibration_v1's 165) -- it is not a claim that 45.5% of unknown ant SPECIES were accepted, and cosine similarity is not calibrated confidence, so these are not 'confidently misidentified' results -- they are closest-match presentations the UI already frames as such, not confirmed identifications.
